correction_author: Codex session, targeted correction before independent review

final_judgment.feedback: The corrections resolve F011 and F012 without contradicting their dependent contracts. All required design checks are true. Earlier resolutions and dismissals remain supported, and no required correction remains open. Acceptance permits phased implementation planning. The specified experiments remain unperformed and are still required before accepting dependent integrations or making release claims.

finding_dispositions.problem: The final-speech fairness rule alternates window units between the latest stopped live run and the oldest waiting run, but the final recognition service holds one resident model inside a 2 GiB charge and D-011 evicts it for a different model. Nothing makes the scheduler residency-aware, so runs pinned to different speech models reload a model at every turn.
finding_dispositions.basis: Custom modes select their own speech model, so a meeting mode on a large model and a dictation mode on a small one is an ordinary configuration. Scenario: a two-hour meeting recognition with model A is queued and the user dictates every minute with model B. The rule as written yields B, B, A, B, B, A with an unload and load at each switch; the charge cannot hold both. Every dictation pays a model load before its first window and the meeting advances one window per two loads. F1 measures reload only within one model, so the failure is not observed before acceptance. State the rule for differing models, for example granting the resident model's run extra windows before switching or bounding switches per interval, and add the mixed-model workload to F1's fairness case.
finding_dispositions.reason: Preserve the resolution. F1 includes repeated dictation on model B alongside meeting recognition on model A, with residency changes and loading costs included in latency and fairness evaluation. The corrections introduce no scheduling change. Additional batching or switch limits still lack supporting measurements.

finding_dispositions.problem: Recognition and diarization checkpoints carry the same validation (input hash, stream, window index, parameters, runtime revision), yet a crash leaves diarization interrupted_resumable while a failed recognition run's checkpoints are reclaimed and an explicit new run recomputes everything. D-004 also routes app-initiated worker termination under capture pressure to that failure policy instead of orderly preemption.
finding_dispositions.basis: Scenario: meeting recognition has committed 230 of 240 windows when the user starts a dictation and memory pressure terminates the final-speech worker. The run fails, 230 validated checkpoints are reclaimed after leases drain, and the retry recomputes two hours of audio. D-031's rationale about reviving stale delivery intent does not apply because recognition publishes to History, not to a target. Either let an explicit retry resume from the last valid checkpoint under the same manifest, or record why recognition checkpoints are less trustworthy than diarization checkpoints. D-031 should also state whether interrupted_resumable resumes automatically at launch or waits for an explicit action, since automatic resume admits a 1.5 GiB job before any user action.
finding_dispositions.reason: Preserve the resolution. D-031 holds checkpointed diarization until explicit Resume, with eligibility validation and normal resource admission. Recognition retains its explicit recomputation policy after crashes or pressure termination. Neither correction changes those policies or supplies grounds to require recognition checkpoint reuse.

finding_dispositions.problem: Every Unicode-route insertion ends unconfirmed because Unicode event success never qualifies as acknowledgment. D-010 says uncertain attempts offer inspection, dismissal or editing, but does not say whether an unconfirmed attempt without a paste barrier retires on its own or stays pending until the user acts.
finding_dispositions.basis: If dismissal is required, each unprofiled dictation costs one action and the remembered Unicode route can never meet F4's 0.1 actions-per-dictation threshold, although the design presents it as the routine option for unprofiled targets. If it retires automatically, uncertain attempts leave the panel and the user may never learn that a silent no-op occurred, which is the failure Apple's Unicode warning describes. State the retirement rule for non-barrier unconfirmed attempts and count it in F4.
finding_dispositions.reason: Preserve the dismissal. D-010 permits independent eligible delivery while an unconfirmed Unicode outcome remains available for inspection. It imposes no mandatory dismissal per Unicode attempt. F4 measures failures and resolution actions, and the corrections do not alter delivery.

finding_dispositions.problem: Clipboard context is sampled within 200 ms of the trigger, and D-010 keeps the previous transcript on the clipboard until barrier retirement. With a remembered paste route and clipboard context enabled, every dictation receives the prior dictation's text as context.
finding_dispositions.basis: Scenario: the user pastes dictation one into Terminal, then dictates again without resolving the barrier. The second run's context contains transcript one; D-012 treats eight-token context copying as advisory only, so the generator can merge or repeat the earlier text, and opt-in retention stores it as an artifact. ClipboardSession already records app ownership through changeCount, so the sampler can recognize its own pending write. State whether app-owned clipboard content is excluded from context or recorded as an omission.
finding_dispositions.reason: Preserve the dismissal. Enabled clipboard context samples current text under D-016's subordinate-authority contract and D-039's retention policy. The specification does not require excluding app-written transcripts. The corrections provide no evidence of a defective sampling contract.

finding_dispositions.problem: Global Escape cancels a live dictation, and D-007 now commits discard on every explicit live cancellation regardless of the interruption preference, with no confirmation or recovery path.
finding_dispositions.basis: Scenario: during a ten-minute dictation into Slack the user presses Escape to close an emoji picker. The dictation is discarded and its verified audio deleted; D-031 offers nothing because discard was committed. Whether the Escape event also reaches the foreground app is unstated, so either the popover stays open, the audio is lost, or both. The spec requires configurable shortcuts and does not require Escape. Make the cancel binding configurable, state whether the event is consumed, and consider confirmation or a brief undo for captures beyond a stated length.
finding_dispositions.reason: Preserve the resolution. Cancellation remains configurable and defaults to no global binding. D-026 defines gesture consumption and pass-through. Its new foreground eligibility rule further limits cancellation of selected processing operations while preserving explicitly configured global cancellation of live dictation. Confirmation or undo is not required by the specification.

finding_dispositions.problem: D-025 applies application-local microphone gain and D-030 records gain and clipping, but neither states whether stored chunks hold pre-gain or post-gain samples.
finding_dispositions.basis: Post-gain storage makes clipping permanent, so a recording made with excessive gain cannot be reprocessed cleanly and the clipping flag is only a diagnosis. Pre-gain storage requires playback and every recognizer window to apply the recorded gain. This is a persistent-data decision the spec says not to defer to implementation; choose one and state the playback and reprocessing consequence.
finding_dispositions.reason: Preserve the resolution. D-030 retains post-gain PCM after saturation and quantization, discloses permanent clipping, and prohibits gain reapplication during playback or reprocessing. The admission-time clarification strengthens that representation contract without changing stored-sample semantics.

finding_dispositions.problem: Screen context capture does not state whether it takes the focused window, the frontmost application's windows or the full display.
finding_dispositions.basis: Full-display capture collects other applications' visible content, such as a password manager or chat window beside the target, supplies it to the model and, with opt-in retention, stores it as an owned artifact. The spec asks the design to define what is sampled and retained for each source. State the capture region and multi-display handling.
finding_dispositions.reason: Preserve the resolution. D-016 specifies isolated capture of the foreground application's focused window, scale normalization across displays, and typed omissions without display fallback. D-039 retains only the supplied representation and metadata. Neither correction changes screen collection.

finding_dispositions.problem: D-041 refers to download catalogs with exact hashes and notices, but nothing states whether the catalog is bundled or fetched, and D-028 authorizes ModelDownloader only for user-requested acquisition of an approved URL.
finding_dispositions.basis: A fetched catalog is a network path outside D-028's contract; an implementation could refresh it at launch and violate the requirement that routine operation needs no network. A bundled catalog goes stale between releases and needs a stated update path. Record the catalog source, its trigger and the process that performs it.
finding_dispositions.reason: Preserve the dismissal. D-028 restricts acquisition networking to explicit user requests and requires routine offline operation. D-041 authorizes no automatic catalog refresh. The corrections create no additional network path.

finding_dispositions.problem: D-001's rationale and assumption 1 state that the Argmax package focuses on Apple Silicon, but ref/RESEARCH.md records only the macOS 14 and Xcode 16 prerequisites.
finding_dispositions.basis: The arm64-only packaging is justified by a claim absent from the supplied evidence. REVIEW_NOTES requires an explicit engineering reason for a first-release hardware limitation. If the package builds and runs on Intel, the exclusion has no stated basis; if it does not, cite the source. Otherwise attribute the choice to the unperformed Intel evaluation rather than to the dependency.
finding_dispositions.reason: Preserve the earlier source-backed dismissal. D-001 states initial arm64 packaging as an engineering choice and identifies the complete-stack evaluation required for Intel support. The gain and cancellation corrections supply no contrary hardware evidence.

finding_dispositions.problem: D-007 names the meeting cancellation control Discard recording, while D-026 names Start Meeting, Stop Meeting and Cancel Meeting, and F5 fixtures use Discard recording.
finding_dispositions.basis: Two names for one control in the authoritative contracts will produce different labels in menu, panel and fixtures. Name it once and reference it.
finding_dispositions.reason: Preserve the dismissal. D-007 specifies Discard recording as the visible label. D-026 references D-007 for the cancellation action's label and semantics, and verification uses that label. The added eligibility rule creates no conflicting label requirement.

finding_dispositions.problem: D-030 applies a gain edit at the next capture chunk boundary and says preview and waveform use that effective gain, but it does not state whether the boundary is fixed when frames are admitted to the ring or when the writer converts them. D-006 allows the writer to fall up to sixty seconds behind admission, so the two readings diverge exactly when a user is most likely to touch the slider.
finding_dispositions.basis: Scenario: an F3-style write stall leaves the writer 30 seconds behind. The user sees a low waveform and raises gain from 1.0 to 2.0. If gain is latched at write time, the chunks written next cover audio admitted 30 seconds earlier; they are saved at 2.0 with permanent saturation, their headers record 2.0, and the waveform showed them at 1.0. If gain is latched at admission time, saved audio matches the display. The chosen representation is post-gain and clipping is irrecoverable, so the ambiguity decides which audio is permanently altered. 'Frame ranges locate gain changes' also sits oddly beside 'each chunk has one effective gain'; if sub-chunk ranges are intended, the per-chunk header field is insufficient, and if not, the sentence adds nothing. State that gain is latched per chunk at admission, independent of writer backlog, and add a gain change during F3's injected stalls to the chunk-boundary-timing check.
finding_dispositions.reason: D-030 now fixes chunk boundaries by admitted native-frame indices and latches gain when each chunk's first frame enters capture storage. Gain is applied once into the bounded Float32 ring. The writer only saturates and quantizes, preserving the latched metadata through retries. Frame ranges explicitly identify whole chunks. This fits D-006's backlog ownership and D-027's existing buffers without another audio queue. F3 now changes gain during injected stalls, including a thirty-second backlog, and checks old versus newly admitted chunks, preview samples, saved samples and retry behavior. The permitted pre-quantization preview difference is explicit. The requested design clarification and verification cases are complete.

finding_dispositions.problem: D-026 makes the global cancellation binding eligible for 'a live dictation or explicitly selected processing operation', and eligible bindings consume the key gesture so the foreground application never receives it. Nothing states whether a processing operation selected in the app's own UI remains 'explicitly selected' while another application is frontmost.
finding_dispositions.basis: Scenario: cancellation is bound to Escape. The user selects a running Note rewrite in History to watch its progress, switches to Slack, and presses Escape to dismiss a popover. Under the text as written the binding matches the selected run, the event is consumed, D-007 discards the incomplete generation output, and Slack keeps its popover open. The user bound Escape expecting it to cancel live dictation, which is the case F5's emoji-picker fixture covers; the fixture does not exercise a selected background operation. Restrict global-binding eligibility to live dictation, or to selected operations only while the app is frontmost, and add the background-selection case to the Escape fixtures so pass-through is verified.
finding_dispositions.reason: D-026 now makes a selected processing operation eligible only when this application is frontmost at the binding's key-down. A retained History selection cannot intercept cancellation in another application when no live dictation exists. Explicitly configured live-dictation cancellation remains global, and an already-owned gesture retains paired-key-up consumption after focus changes. D-007's stage-specific cancellation effects remain intact. Verification now covers a selected running operation followed by switching applications, foreground and live-dictation cases, disabled cancellation, and focus changes between key-down and key-up.
